body_text:
Riemann's Removable Singularity Theorem.

Let $f$ be holomorphic on a punctured disk $D^*(z_0, r)$. The singularity at $z_0$ is removable
if and only if $f$ is bounded in a punctured neighborhood of $z_0$:
$$ \sup_{0 < |z - z_0| < \delta} |f(z)| < \infty \quad \text{for some } \delta > 0. $$

*Proof*: If $z_0$ is removable, $f$ extends continuously to $z_0$, hence is bounded near $z_0$.
Conversely, assume $|f(z)| \le M$ on $D^*(z_0, \delta)$. For any $n \ge 1$, the Laurent coefficient $a_{-n}$
is given on a circle of radius $\rho < \delta$ by:
$$ a_{-n} = \frac{1}{2\pi i} \oint_{|z - z_0| = \rho} f(z)(z - z_0)^{n-1}\,dz. $$
Applying the $ML$-inequality:
$$ |a_{-n}| \le \frac{1}{2\pi} \cdot M \rho^{n-1} \cdot (2\pi\rho) = M \rho^n. $$
Taking $\rho \to 0$ forces $a_{-n} = 0$ for all $n \ge 1$. Thus the principal part vanishes identically,
and $f$ extends holomorphically across $z_0$.
